meta.titre: Absorption in the Ileum: villus adaptations and the journey of glucose
meta.sous_theme: Adaptations of the ileum and the route of absorbed food

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Human Biology past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A student in Garoua eats a plate of rice and fish before an afternoon exam and expects the energy to reach her brain in time. The meal only becomes useful once its digested parts pass through the wall of the gut into the blood. This happens mainly in the last part of the small intestine, the ileum. GCE papers ask you to outline how the ileum is built for absorption and to trace where an absorbed molecule goes next, so both the structure and the route must be learnt.

items: Digestion changes large food molecules into small soluble ones such as glucose, amino acids, fatty acids and glycerol.
Diffusion is the movement of particles from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration.
The heart pumps blood through arteries, capillaries and veins in a double circulation.

sections.titre: Adaptations of the ileum and fate of absorbed food
sections.contenu_markdown:
### What is absorbed
**Absorption** is the movement of digested food from the gut into the blood or lymph. It happens mostly in the ileum. Glucose, amino acids, vitamins and mineral salts pass into the blood capillaries. Fatty acids and glycerol pass into the lymph. Most water is also absorbed in the small intestine. Absorption takes place by **diffusion** and by **active transport**, which uses energy to move molecules (such as glucose) against a concentration gradient.

### Adaptations of the ileum

| Adaptation | How it helps absorption |
|---|---|
| Long, narrow tube | Food stays for a long time in contact with the wall |
| Folds and many finger-like **villi** | Greatly increase surface area |
| **Microvilli** on the free surface of the epithelial cells | Increase the area even further |
| Wall of a villus only one cell thick | Short distance for diffusion |
| Dense network of blood capillaries in each villus | Carries absorbed food away quickly, so a steep concentration gradient is kept |
| A lacteal in each villus | Takes up fatty acids and glycerol |
| Many mitochondria in the epithelial cells | Supply energy for active transport |
| Goblet cells | Make mucus that protects and lubricates the wall |

### Route of absorbed food
Glucose and amino acids pass into the capillaries of the villus, which join to form the **hepatic portal vein**. This vein carries blood to the **liver**, which controls the amount of glucose and amino acids sent on, and stores extra glucose as glycogen. Blood leaves the liver by the **hepatic vein**, which joins the vena cava and reaches the heart.

variantes.nom: Tracing glucose to a body organ
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked how an absorbed molecule gets to the brain or to a muscle
variantes.contenu_markdown: Villus capillaries, hepatic portal vein, liver, hepatic vein, vena cava, right atrium, right ventricle, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary vein, left atrium, left ventricle, aorta, an artery to the organ (the carotid arteries for the brain), capillaries in the organ. There glucose diffuses into the cells, where it is used in respiration to release energy. Always mention the liver and the heart on the way.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a mark scheme gives one mark for each adaptation and its effect
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give each adaptation together with its effect, not the name alone: "thin wall, so a short diffusion distance". Do not describe digestion. The villi do not digest food and do not move it along; they absorb. Choose structures that are clearly linked to a function, and make sure the number of points matches the marks.

sections.enonce_markdown: Describe how an amino acid from a digested piece of fish is carried from the ileum to a muscle cell in the leg, and name two features of a villus that help it to be absorbed quickly. *(6 marks)*

etapes.justification: "Describe how" needs the route in order, and "name two features" needs two adaptations with effects.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Part 1: route from ileum to leg muscle. Part 2: two villus features.

etapes.justification: Amino acids go into the blood, not the lymph.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The amino acid is absorbed into a blood capillary of a villus.

etapes.justification: All blood from the gut goes first to the liver by the hepatic portal vein, then returns to the heart and passes through the lungs.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Hepatic portal vein, liver, hepatic vein, vena cava, right atrium, right ventricle, lungs, left atrium, left ventricle.

etapes.justification: Blood leaves the heart by the aorta and an artery branches towards the leg.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Aorta, an artery to the leg, capillaries in the muscle, where the amino acid enters the muscle cell.

etapes.justification: Pair each feature with its effect.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Wall one cell thick (short diffusion distance); dense capillary network (keeps a steep concentration gradient).

sections.conclusion_markdown: The amino acid is absorbed into a blood capillary in a villus, travels in the hepatic portal vein to the liver, then through the hepatic vein and vena cava to the right side of the heart. It passes through the lungs to the left side of the heart and leaves in the aorta, reaching the leg muscle through an artery and its capillaries, where it enters the cells. A villus is quick at absorbing because its wall is one cell thick, giving a short diffusion distance, and because a dense network of capillaries carries the amino acids away and keeps a steep concentration gradient.

items.erreur_markdown: Villi digest the food in the ileum.
items.pourquoi_faux: Digestion is done by enzymes in the juices of the gut; villi are folds of the wall that increase the area for absorption.
items.correction_markdown: Villi **absorb**; enzymes in the intestinal and pancreatic juices **digest**.

items.erreur_markdown: All the digested food is absorbed into blood capillaries.
items.pourquoi_faux: Fatty acids and glycerol are taken up mainly by the lacteal, which is a lymph vessel.
items.correction_markdown: Glucose and amino acids enter the blood; fatty acids and glycerol enter the lymph.

items.erreur_markdown: Blood carrying glucose goes straight from the ileum to the heart.
items.pourquoi_faux: The blood from the gut first goes through the hepatic portal vein to the liver.
items.correction_markdown: Ileum, hepatic portal vein, **liver**, hepatic vein, vena cava, heart.

items.erreur_markdown: Starch and protein molecules are absorbed through the villi.
items.pourquoi_faux: They are too large to pass through the wall of the gut. They must first be digested to glucose and amino acids.
items.correction_markdown: Only the small soluble end products of digestion are absorbed.

items.enonce_markdown: State the part of a villus that (a) takes up fatty acids and glycerol and (b) takes up glucose. Name two other substances absorbed in the small intestine.
items.solution_markdown: (a) The **lacteal**. (b) The **blood capillaries**. Other substances absorbed: any two of water, mineral salts, vitamins, amino acids.

items.enonce_markdown: In a model, a 2 cm length of smooth ileum lining has an area of 12 cm$^2$. Folds make the area 3 times larger, the villi make it a further 10 times larger, and the microvilli make it a further 20 times larger. (a) Calculate the final area in cm$^2$. (b) How many times larger is it than the smooth lining? (c) Explain why a large area helps absorption.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $12 \times 3 \times 10 \times 20 =$ **7200 cm$^2$**.

(b) $7200 \div 12 =$ **600 times**.

(c) More surface is in contact with the digested food, so more molecules can be absorbed in a given time.

items.enonce_markdown: A child suffers from a disease that damages and flattens the villi of the ileum. Predict and explain two effects on the child's health.
items.solution_markdown:
Award a mark for each effect with its reason, for example:

- The child loses weight and lacks energy, because the surface area for absorption is much smaller, so less glucose and fat is absorbed.
- The child grows poorly or is weak, because fewer amino acids, vitamins and mineral salts reach the blood, so protein synthesis and growth are reduced.
- Undigested or unabsorbed food passes on to the large intestine and may cause diarrhoea.

items_markdown: Absorption is the passage of digested food into the blood or lymph, mainly in the ileum, by diffusion and active transport.
Adaptations: long tube, folds, villi, microvilli, wall one cell thick, dense capillaries, lacteal, many mitochondria; always give the effect with each.
Glucose and amino acids go into blood capillaries; fatty acids and glycerol go into the lacteal.
Blood from the ileum goes by the hepatic portal vein to the liver, then to the heart, lungs, heart again and the body.
Villi absorb; they do not digest.
